seo.description: Visit the Zegzel Valley and Beni Snassen mountains near Oujda: green valleys, prehistoric caves, hiking and a perfect nature day trip from the city.
seo.og_description: Green valleys, caves and mountain air less than an hour from Oujda – the best nature escape in the Oriental.

name: Vallée de Zegzel & Beni Snassen
hero_subtitle: Green valleys, prehistoric caves and mountain scenery in the Beni Snassen range – the classic nature day trip from Oujda.

overview.title: The Green Side of the Oriental
overview.p1: The Vallée de Zegzel lies in the Beni Snassen mountains, a short drive from Oujda. After the dry plains around the city, the valley appears almost unexpectedly green, with orchards, streams and shaded paths. It is the favourite nature escape for locals and one of the most rewarding day trips in the region.
overview.p2: The area is also known for its prehistoric caves, including the famous Grotte du Chameau and other cavities that have yielded important archaeological finds. Hiking trails of varying difficulty offer views over the surrounding hills.
overview.p3: A full day allows time for a cave visit, a short walk and a simple lunch in the valley. In spring the landscape is at its greenest; in autumn the temperatures are ideal for walking.

moods.title: How to Spend the Day
moods.subtitle: A flexible half-day or full-day outing.

1.title: Leave Oujda Early
1.desc: Drive or take a taxi to the valley while it is still cool. Start with a cave visit or a short walk.

2.title: Walk and Picnic
2.desc: Explore a trail, rest by the water and have a simple lunch in the shade or at a local café.

3.title: Return via Viewpoints
3.desc: Take a last look from a higher point, then head back to Oujda before dark.

food.title: What to Eat in the Valley
food.p1: Options are simple and local. Many visitors bring a picnic; others stop at small cafés or restaurants in the area.
food.li1: Picnic by the stream or under the trees.
food.li2: Simple grills and tagines at local eateries when open.
food.li3: Fresh bread, olives and fruit bought in Oujda before leaving.
food.li4: Mint tea at a roadside café.
food.li5: Return to Oujda for a fuller dinner if preferred.
food.p2: Bring enough water. In summer the valley can still be warm, and facilities are limited.

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: About 40–50 km from Oujda (roughly 1 hour). Grand taxi, private driver or organised tour. A car gives the most flexibility for viewpoints and short walks.

2.title: What to Bring
2.desc: Walking shoes, sun protection, water, a light picnic and a torch if you plan to enter caves.

3.title: Caves
3.desc: Some caves have modest entry fees and basic facilities. Opening can depend on the season and local guides – ask in Oujda or on arrival.

q1.question: How far is Zegzel from Oujda?
q1.answer: Approximately 40–50 km, or about one hour by car or taxi depending on the exact destination in the valley.

q2.question: Do I need a guide for the caves?
q2.answer: A local guide is useful and sometimes required for the more interesting caves. Ask in Oujda or on arrival.

q3.question: Is it suitable for children?
q3.answer: Yes for the valley floor and short walks. Some cave passages and steeper trails may not suit very young children.

q4.question: What is the best season?
q4.answer: Spring (March–May) for greenery and mild temperatures; autumn (September–November) for comfortable walking weather.

q5.question: Can I combine Zegzel with Saïdia on the same day?
q5.answer: It is possible but rushed. Better to keep Zegzel as a nature day and Saïdia as a separate beach day.
